For hot flashes and other menopause symptoms: the FDA-approved medicines, and what compounded hormones are.

The FDA-approved options are estradiol, alone or with progesterone, and one non-hormonal pill. Compounded hormones are not FDA approved.

  • Compounded hormones · pharmacy-made hormones from online clinicsNot FDA approved; pharmacy-madeon prescription

    Hormones made by a pharmacy and sold by some online clinics, not FDA approved.

    Hormones a pharmacy makes itself. The FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold. 106

    Not FDA approved; pharmacy-made.

    Prescription through the clinic.

    On prescription; no clinic prices yet
  • Estradiol (pill, patch or gel) · estrogen pill, patch or gel for hot flashesFDA approvedon prescription

    An estrogen taken as a pill, patch or gel, FDA approved for hot flashes due to menopause.

    Replaces estrogen, which falls at menopause. In a woman with a uterus, estrogen alone raises the risk of endometrial cancer. 101, 102, 103

    FDA approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.

    Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor.

    On prescription; no clinic prices yet
  • Estradiol with progesterone (Bijuva) · one capsule with both hormonesFDA approvedon prescription

    One capsule with both hormones, FDA approved for hot flashes in women with a uterus.

    One capsule each evening with food, with an estrogen and progesterone in it. For women with a uterus. 104

    FDA approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, in women with a uterus.

    Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor.

    On prescription; no clinic prices yet
  • Fezolinetant (Veozah) · non-hormonal daily pill for hot flashesFDA approvedon prescription

    A daily non-hormonal pill, FDA approved for hot flashes due to menopause.

    One pill a day with no hormone in it. Its label warns of liver injury, so it needs liver blood tests before and during treatment. 105

    FDA approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.

    Prescription, with liver blood tests before and during treatment.

    On prescription; no clinic prices yet
